newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent holds gains, gas oil cuts losses.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent holds gains, gas oil cuts losses.

text.p: IPE Brent crude futures held their morning gains in afternoon business on Thursday but failed to move higher in lacklustre trade.
July Brent was up 25 cents at $17.60 a barrel by 1445 GMT. July gas oil was 75 cents lower at $163 a tonne after the June contract expired at $162.25.
"We've bounced up a little bit from yesterday's lows. The market is holding up fairly well but it's rangebound," one trader said. "There is nothing too much going on."
Market sentiment was rather stymied as players recovered from a fall in the Brent price late on Wednesday to $17.32.
Traders were also waiting for news on resumed Iraqi oil sales amid speculation of a slow start to the next six months of the U.N./Iraq oil-for-food deal.
The chairman of the U.N. Sanctions Committee said Baghdad was awaiting procedures to be agreed for implementing a new distribution plan before proposing its oil prices.
But brokers said the news had been priced into the market for now. "People are watching the story but they are not taking too much notice," one said.
Gas oil, meanwhile, was in consolidatory form and holding up after it retraced Wednesday's late Brent falls in morning trade.
Though the June contract expiry had run out fairly smoothly, brokers said the market tone remained bearish.
The IPE said earlier that the delivery against the expired June gas oil contract would be 1,360 lots or 136,000 tonnes, compared with last month's 97,100 tonnes delivered into the May contract.
Dealers had been expecting a far smaller volume.
And official data showing Singapore's weekly middle distillates at the highest level since at least January 1994 enhanced the weak outlook for gas oil, they said.
